what_its_for: Dutasteride is used to treat an enlarged prostate gland (called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH) in men. It helps shrink the prostate over time, which can make it easier to urinate, reduce the urge to urinate frequently, and lower the risk of needing prostate surgery.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, chew, or open the capsule — the medicine inside can irritate your mouth and throat. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual dose is one 0.5 mg capsule taken by mouth once a day. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store dutasteride at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Women who are pregnant or could become pregnant must NOT touch or handle dutasteride capsules. If a pregnant woman absorbs this medicine through her skin, it can cause serious birth defects in a male baby. If contact occurs, wash the area immediately with soap and water. Do not donate blood while taking dutasteride or for at least 6 months after stopping, because this medicine could harm a pregnant woman who receives your blood. Avoid drinking grapefruit juice in large amounts, as it may affect how the medicine works. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about all other medicines you take, including vitamins and herbal supplements.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice: breast lumps, breast pain, or nipple discharge (these could be signs of a rare breast condition); trouble urinating or no urine output at all; skin rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, or throat (signs of an allergic reaction); or any changes in your mood or signs of depression. Also tell your doctor if you experience a decreased sex drive, trouble getting or maintaining an erection, or problems with ejaculation, as these side effects can sometimes persist even after stopping the medicine.
when_it_works: Dutasteride works slowly. It may take 3 to 6 months or longer before you notice an improvement in your symptoms. Do not stop taking it just because you do not feel different right away. Keep taking it as prescribed and discuss any concerns with your doctor at your follow-up visits.
special_populations: This medicine is for use by MEN ONLY. Women and children should never take dutasteride. Pregnant women must not handle the capsules at all. If you have liver disease, tell your doctor before taking this medicine, as dutasteride is processed by the liver and dose adjustments or extra monitoring may be needed. Older adults (over 65) can take this medicine safely, but should report any side effects to their doctor promptly.
